en.title: Amazon's Muhammad Ali Series: A Sturdy Retelling Fans Have Seen Before
en.summary: Amazon's new limited series, **The Greatest**, aims to repackage the life of boxing legend **Muhammad Ali** for a new generation. While it boasts the backing of Ali's estate and a focus on his brother's perspective, early reviews suggest a familiar narrative arc.
en.body:
Amazon Prime Video is stepping into the ring with **The Greatest**, a new limited series charting the extraordinary life of **Muhammad Ali**. Created by **Ben Watkins** and executive produced by **Lonnie Ali** and **Michael B. Jordan**, the show features **Jaalen Best** in the titular role. It promises a comprehensive look at the boxing icon's journey, from his meteoric rise to his exile from the sport and his triumphant, albeit challenging, late-career comebacks. The series also touches upon his resilience in the face of Parkinson's disease, a cause he championed until his passing.

While the series is billed as the first 'authorized scripted series' and draws heavily from the perspective of Ali's brother, **Rahaman Ali**, early critical reception suggests a sense of déjà vu. The Guardian's review notes that while there are 'small pleasures to be had in this straightforward retelling,' the narrative tread is well-worn. For viewers intimately familiar with Ali's life through countless documentaries, biographies, and previous dramatizations, **The Greatest** may feel like a story told too many times. The challenge for **Amazon MGM Studios** lies in adding a unique spin or uncovering untold nuances within a life that has already been extensively documented and celebrated.

## A Familiar Fight Card
The series' premise, based on the life of a public figure as globally recognized as **Muhammad Ali**, is inherently broad. The collaboration with Ali's estate, and specifically his widow **Lonnie Ali**, lends an air of authenticity. However, the decision to lean on **Rahaman Ali**'s perspective, while offering an intimate viewpoint, might inadvertently reinforce the established narrative. This approach risks presenting a 'greatest hits' compilation rather than a deeply revelatory exploration. The question for fans will be whether **The Greatest** offers enough new insight to justify its existence alongside the rich tapestry of existing **Muhammad Ali** content, or if it's simply a sturdy, if somewhat redundant, addition to his cinematic legacy.

## What's Next for Ali's Story
Fans eager to see **Jaalen Best** step into the shoes of the legendary boxer will have to wait until November 4, 2026, for the premiere of **The Greatest** on Amazon Prime Video. With the series set to debut in late 2026, the landscape of television will undoubtedly have shifted. It remains to be seen how this biographical drama will stand out against other critically acclaimed series that may emerge in the preceding months, such as HBO's **Half Man** or the continued animation triumphs of **Primal**.

content_raw: There are small pleasures to be had in this straightforward retelling of the boxing champ’s life but there’s not much most viewers haven’t seen before The Greatest is a new limited series that repackages the life of Muhammad Ali for generations born too late to remember when the sporting icon was the world’s most famous man, or too lazy to seek out one of the many books written about his boxing rise, his exile from the sport for refusing the draft, his improbable late-career comeback and his steely resilience in the face of a seismic Parkinson’s diagnosis . That this TV adaptation comes from Amazon is both a stroke of vertical integration and an indictment of a viewing public whose patience for source material wears thinner with every scroll. The Prime Video drama says it’s based on “the life of Muhammad Ali”, a credible claim given the extent to which Ali’s cultural ubiquity made him a public figure of eminent domain. The first-ever “authorized scripted series” also has the backing of Ali’s widow, Lonnie, who serves as an executive producer. But the show clearly takes its direction from the definitive tome authored by Muhammad Ali’s brother, Rahaman Ali. The younger brother was a lifelong sparring partner, sharing a room in their childhood Kentucky home and remaining a prominent member of his entourage until the champ’s death in 2016, aged 74 – an occasion for global mourning .
